page: Amazon Web Services r8g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit Arm Neoverse-V2 AWS Graviton4 processors. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking throughput delivers a 40 Gbps baseline connection. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements show top-tier multi-core compute and memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 163,577.25, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,981.0, both placing in the top ten percent of tested servers. Memory throughput is a key highlight, delivering 481.11 GB/sec on large-block uncached reads and 217.98 GB/sec on large-block writes. Single-core performance occupies the middle tier, with Geekbench single-core registering 1,885.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1,706.4.

The combination of 96 physical cores and 768 GB of high-bandwidth memory drives strong results in data-intensive tasks. In-memory database performance reached 195.4 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while PassMark database operations scored 47,367.65. Software compilation in Clang and static web serving throughput also achieved top-decile ratings at 94,490.0 and 154.42 GB/sec respectively. In large language model CPU inference, the architecture maintains strong text generation rates of 46.93 tokens per second on 7B models and 7.13 tokens per second on 70B models.

Cost efficiency is favorable for workloads capable of leveraging high memory density and non-hyperthreaded Arm cores. Because the 96 vCPUs map directly to 96 physical cores, resource contention is minimized. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, alongside average single-threaded execution speeds. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases like Redis, extensive caching layers, distributed data analytics, ETL pipelines, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit Arm Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.8 GHz, managed by the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8.0 GB per-core allocation supported by high uncached read bandwidth of 481.11 GB/sec. The instance delivers a 40 Gbps baseline network capacity, omitting local storage and hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top ten percent for multi-core compute, Clang compilation, and in-memory key-value processing, evidenced by 195.4 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread throughput falls in the median range and persistent workloads require remote block storage, its dense memory capacity and dedicated core allocation deliver efficient resource utilization for in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale enterprise services.
